sources.title: Call of Duty publisher apologizes for using real footage of Itaewon crowd crush | Yonhap News Agency
sources.text:
Call of Duty publisher apologizes for using real footage of Itaewon crowd crush | Yonhap News Agency Go to Contents Go to Navigation Facebook X More Pinterest Linked in Tumblr Reddit Facebook Messenger Copy URL URL is copied. OK SEOUL, Oct. 30 (Yonhap) -- The makers behind the Call of Duty video game apologized Friday for using real footage of the deadly 2022 Seoul crowd crush in its latest installment of the game and agreed to remove the footage. A short clip showing a paramedic performing CPR on a crowd crush victim lying on the street appeared in the opening moments of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. The footage was used to depict a scenario of civilian casualties during a fictional war with North Korea. "We deeply apologize to the victims and their bereaved families who must have suffered, as well as to everyone who we have caused concern," Activision Publishing Inc. said in a notice to local reporters. "The footage will be removed in our update set to be rolled out on Nov. 12." The publisher added it had no plans to evoke tragic events, including the Itaewon crowd crush, when using news footage in its games, nor had it intended to ignore the pain caused by the accident. A total of 159 people were killed in a narrow alleyway in Seoul's night life district of Itaewon during Halloween festivities on Oct. 29, 2022. Bereaved families of the victims have criticized the game publisher for "lacking common sense" by using such footage and demanded a complete removal of the clip. A screen capture from the Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 game, which featured real footage of the Itaewon crowd crush that claimed the lives of 159 people on Oct. 29, 2022. claims.text: Activision Publishing used real footage of the 2022 Seoul Itaewon crowd crush in the opening moments of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4.
The footage depicted a paramedic performing CPR on a crowd crush victim and was used to portray civilian casualties during a fictional war with North Korea.
Activision Publishing apologized for the use of the footage and agreed to remove it in an update scheduled for November 12, 2026.

The Itaewon crowd crush resulted in 159 deaths on October 29, 2022.

letters.subject: Request for Information Regarding Activision Publishing Use of Itaewon Crowd Crush Footage
letters.body:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We are PLAIN., the investigative desk of plain-news.ch, an independent, advertising‑free Swiss news site. Our research is AI‑assisted and reviewed by a human editor. We are investigating whether the US game developer Activision Publishing used footage of the 2022 Seoul Itaewon crowd crush in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 and the subsequent actions taken.

1. Did Activision Publishing obtain the footage of the 2022 Seoul Itaewon crowd crush from a licensed source or through a third‑party provider?
2. What, if any, payment or compensation did Activision Publishing provide to the owners of the footage used in the game?
3. On what date did Activision Publishing announce the removal of the footage, and what was the scheduled release date for the update that removed it?
4. Has the US Department of Justice received any complaints or filed any action regarding this matter?

We will publish your reply; you may choose to provide a full or summarized response. If any fact is incorrect, we welcome corrections.

Please respond by 4 November 2026.

Sincerely,
PLAIN. Investigative desk
desk@plain-news.ch

This research is AI-assisted. Every text is reviewed by a human editor before it is published.

letters.subject: Request for Information Regarding Call of Duty Content
letters.body:
Dear Infinity Ward and Sledgehammer Games,

We are the investigative desk of PLAIN. (plain-news.ch), an independent, advertising‑free Swiss news outlet. Our research is AI‑assisted and reviewed by a human editor. We are currently examining the use of footage from the 2022 Seoul Itaewon crowd crush in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 and the subsequent actions taken by your publisher.

1. Did Infinity Ward or Sledgehammer Games have any role in selecting or approving the footage of the Itaewon crowd crush used in the opening sequence of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4? 2. When was the decision made to remove the footage, and what was the timeline for the update scheduled for November 12, 2026? 3. What internal policies or guidelines were consulted to determine that the footage would not evoke tragic events, including the Itaewon crowd crush? 4. Were any compensatory measures discussed or offered to the families of the victims? 5. Has any communication been sent to the bereaved families regarding the removal of the clip?

We will publish your response in full or in summary, at your discretion. If any fact in our inquiry is incorrect, please let us know so we can correct it. Kindly provide your answers by 4 November 2026.

Sincerely,
PLAIN. Investigative desk
desk@plain-news.ch
